quick_skim.title: Distillation for Efficient Multitask Manipulation Policies via Conditional Flow Matching
quick_skim.abstract: Advances in generative modeling have recently been extensively employed in robotics for policy learning. In particular, Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) trained with expert demonstrations has been shown to outperform existing methods on robot manipulation benchmarks. While prior work has mainly focused on single-task settings, we study the problem from a multi-task perspective, as training independent models for each task is computationally expensive. Multi-Task policy learning comes with its own set of challenges, as naively training on a concatenated dataset of demonstrations would either require increased model capacity to accommodate the added complexity or result in drops in performance. We propose to distill knowledge from single-task CFM experts into a shared multi-task policy by transferring their learned velocity fields. We combine this distillation signal with the original CFM objective to retain fidelity to the demonstrations. Experiments on RLBench show that our approach improves multi-task policy performance over naive training while maintaining a fixed model size.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: This paper addresses efficient multi-task robot policy learning, proposing to distill knowledge from single-task Conditional Flow Matching experts. It shows that generative flow matching can be adapted to multitask manipulation without costly per-task models.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 本文针对多任务机器人操作策略训练成本高的问题，提出利用条件流匹配（CFM）从单任务专家中蒸馏知识。方法将生成式流匹配扩展到多任务设置，避免为每个任务独立训练模型，缓解拼接数据带来的性能下降。实验表明该蒸馏框架在操作基准上保持高效且性能良好，为生成式建模在机器人策略学习中的可扩展应用提供了新思路。

quick_skim.title: ReaFlow-TTS: Realization-Conditioned Flow Matching for High-Quality and Controllable Speech Synthesis
quick_skim.abstract: In flow-matching text-to-speech (TTS), different speech realizations can induce different target velocities under the same generation conditions. A deterministic velocity field trained with squared error predicts their conditional mean, thereby marginalizing realization-dependent variation. Meanwhile, modeling such variation does not inherently provide a semantically interpretable interface for attribute manipulation. We propose ReaFlow-TTS, a realization-conditioned flow-matching framework that introduces an utterance-level stochastic realization latent and uses it to condition velocity prediction throughout the generation trajectory. We further impose valence-arousal-dominance (VAD) semantics on the realization space, enabling direct and graded attribute manipulation without target speech at inference. Experiments demonstrate improved synthesis quality over a matched full-mask baseline and reproducible latent-induced pitch, energy, and timing tendencies across initial-noise samples, providing behavioral evidence that the latent is used as a reusable realization condition. Subjective evaluation further demonstrates graded VAD manipulation across generation contexts with only modest changes in naturalness.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: ReaFlow-TTS conditions a flow-matching TTS velocity field on an utterance-level stochastic realization latent with VAD semantics, improving synthesis quality and controllable attribute manipulation.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对流匹配语音合成中同一条件下不同语音实现导致速度场只能预测条件均值、损失实现层差异且缺乏可解释控制接口的问题，本文提出实现条件流匹配框架，引入话语级随机实现隐变量并在整条生成轨迹上条件化速度预测，同时将VAD语义施加于实现空间。实验表明该方法在保持高合成质量的同时实现了对语音属性的可控调节，说明显式建模实现层随机性可兼顾生成质量与可控性。

quick_skim.title: Faster Visuomotor Policy Learning on Action Manifolds via Riemannian MeanFlow
quick_skim.abstract: Visuomotor policies learn a direct map from raw sensory observations to robot action sequences. Policies based on Diffusion and Flow Matching capture the multimodal distribution over action sequences in an end-to-end manner. This expressivity comes at the cost of multi-step numerical integration of the learned vector field for action generation, which can be expensive and time-consuming, impeding fast control rates required in robotics applications. Furthermore, robot action sequences are usually defined on a smooth, differentiable manifold, requiring that the learned policy respects the intrinsic geometry of the robot's action space. Here, we present Riemannian MeanFlow Policy (RMFP), which learns the conditioned flow map of the probability path on the robot action manifold. Our formulation employs a flow map consistency objective grounded in the data by a Riemannian Conditional Flow Matching anchor. The flow map consistency condition is stable to train and constrains the learned model to finite-time transport, which yields on-manifold action sequence generation with as few as one network function evaluation. We present results on the spherical LASA and Push-T benchmarks, on the Tool Hang and Transport tasks of the Robomimic suite, and on the Franka Kitchen task with manifold-constrained action generation, and demonstrate that RMFP attains performance competitive with prior work at a lower sampling cost. We also employ RMFP on a real-world robotic manipulation task to demonstrate fast action generation under imperfect sensor measurements in the physical world.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 视觉运动策略学习从原始观测到机器人动作序列的直接映射，基于扩散与流匹配的策略能端到端刻画动作序列的多模态分布，但需对学习到的向量场做多步数值积分，代价高昂且难以满足机器人所需的快速控制频率，同时动作序列通常位于光滑可微流形上，要求策略尊重动作空间的内在几何。本文提出黎曼MeanFlow策略RMFP，学习概率路径的条件流映射。该工作在保持多模态表达能力的同时显著加速了策略生成。
